items.nl: A one-unit full-data PROBABILITY law \(P\) for \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\) on the Borel product space \(\{1,\dots,k\}\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathbb R^{d_z}\times\mathbb R^3\), with fixed known latent cardinality \(k\ge 2\) and fixed proxy dimensions \(d_x,d_z\ge k\).  The latent-class masses are \(p_u:=P(U=u)\), the latent conditional potential-outcome means are \(\mu_{tu}:=E_P[Y(t)\mid U=u]\) with latent-class effects \(\tau_u:=\mu_{1u}-\mu_{0u}\) (common value \(\tau_\star\) under homogeneity), the proxy feature matrices are \(A_t(:,u):=E_P[Z\mid U=u,T=t]\in\mathbb R^{d_z\times k}\) and \(B(:,u):=E_P[X\mid U=u]\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\), and \(e_1\) is the first canonical basis vector of \(\mathbb R^{d_x}\).  The observed record is \(O=(T,X,Z,Y)\), and the observed margin \(P_O\) is the marginalization of \(P\) along \(w\mapsto O\), i.e. the pushforward \(P\circ O^{-1}\), which is again a probability law.  The uniformly conditioned causal VMW submodel \(\mathcal M\) is the set of such \(P\) satisfying the ten member conditions of \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\) at the fixed margins \(L\ge1\), \(\pi_0\in(0,1/(2k)]\), \(\sigma_0\in(0,1]\), with derived effect-support radius \(L_\tau:=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\); \(\mathcal M(g)\) is its gap-localized stratum at nearest-effect gap \(\delta(P)\) of order \(g\in(0,1/4]\). — SURVEY (Causalean/PO/, Causalean/SCM/): `Causalean.PO.POSystem` (PO/Core/System.lean, API.md §8h) is a regime-indexed evaluation structure `{V, X, Omega, mu, eval}` built for multi-node `Regime`-based interventions, with `PO/Assumptions/Consistency.lean` and `PO/Assumptions/IndepCF.lean` supplying `POSystem.Consistency` and counterfactual independence at that abstraction; API.md records the PO layer as a partly-sorry skeleton. BYPASS-JUSTIFIED: this note's object is ONE law on a fixed 7-fold Borel product with a LATENT (unobserved, finitely valued) confounder and a binary treatment, and every single proof step works with explicit conditional first and second moments on the finitely many latent-arm cells \(\{U=u,T=t\}\) plus the matrix factorisations \(M_t=A_tD_tB^\top\), \(N_t=A_tD_t\mathrm{diag}(\mu_t)B^\top\).  `POSystem` supplies no conditional-moment or matrix layer, its regime/`fixSet` machinery is entirely unused here, and routing through it would force a `ValuesOn`-indexed encoding of every matrix identity.  We therefore scaffold the world directly over Mathlib measures, importing `Causalean.Mathlib.CondIndep`/`Indep` only for the CondIndepFun re-exports named in D-plan-2. Armwise counts are \(N_{t,n}:=\sum_i\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}\); the total Borel empirical summary \(\widehat S_n:=(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},\widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},\widehat m_{X,n})\) divides by \(\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}\) and is the zero matrix on an empty arm.  Inference runs at miscoverage \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) or generic tail level \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), through the simultaneous radius \(r_{n,\alpha}:=C_0L\sqrt{\log(C_0/\alpha)/n}\) and the concentration event \(E_P:=\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))\le r_{n,\alpha}\}\), with \(C_0\) depending only on \(k,d_x,d_z,\pi_0,\sigma_0\). — PROBABILITY INSTANCES (round-4 correction, per D-plan-8 - read this FIRST, every reuse below depends on it): each of the four decls this world routes through binds an `IsProbabilityMeasure` instance on its measure argument, verified in source - `Causalean.Stat.iidSample_infinitePi (P : Measure X) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]` (PiTransport.lean:54), `Causalean.Stat.pinskerBound_pi_iid (μ ν) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]` (Pinsker.lean:449), `Causalean.Mathlib.InformationTheory.productKL_tensorization_of_finite (n) (μ ν) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]` (ProductKLLeCam.lean:379), `pi_iid_llr_integrable (μ ν) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]` (:452).  `iidSample_finN_pushforward` / `event_pullback_along_iidSample` do not bind one themselves but are only ever applied to `S := iidSample_infinitePi (obsLaw P)`, so they inherit the requirement. items.label: Definition P-3
items.nl: For \(N_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}\), set \(\widehat M_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Z_iX_i^\top/\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}\), \(\widehat N_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Y_iZ_iX_i^\top/\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}\), \(\widehat m_{X,n}:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i\), and \(\widehat S_n:=(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},\widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},\widehat m_{X,n})\). Both armwise matrices are the zero matrix on \(\{N_{t,n}=0\}\), so \(\widehat S_n\) is a total Borel function of the sample.

items.label: Definition P-10
items.nl:
For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0,\alpha,C_0,C_{\mathrm{lat}}\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(0<k\), \(0<n\), \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), \(0<\alpha<1/2\), \(1\le C_0\), and \(0<C_{\mathrm{lat}}\), put \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\) and assume \(0\le L_\tau\). Fix an observed sample \(\omega\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\) with empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\), and set
\[r_{n,\alpha}:=C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}}.\]
Let \((\overline F,\Pi)\) be repair data on the closure \(\mathcal K\): \(\overline F\) is continuous on \(\mathcal K\) and extends the summary-to-quotient-law map on model summaries, \(\Pi\) is measurable, \(\Pi(s)\in\mathcal K\) minimizes \(d_S(\cdot,s)\) over \(\mathcal K\) whenever \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\), \(\Pi(s)=0\) whenever \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), and the induced repaired estimator is measurable. Let \(\widehat\lambda_n\) be the valid \(k\)-atomic law returned at \(\omega\) by a measurable prescribed structured-lattice estimator at support radius \(L_\tau\), generated by an exhaustive duplicate-free lexicographically ordered list of well-formed \(H_n,q_n\) lattice candidates and the first lexicographic minimizer of \(J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)\) with threshold \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\). Define
\[\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}:=\begin{cases}\{\overline F(q):q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le2r_{n,\alpha}\},&\mathcal K\ne\varnothing,\\\{\delta_0\},&\mathcal K=\varnothing,\end{cases}\]
put \(m_\star:=\pi_0\) and \(R_{n,\alpha}:=C_{\mathrm{lat}}(r_{n,\alpha}+(\sqrt n)^{-1})\), and define
\[\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_\tau,L_\tau]):=\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau]):\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m_\star,\xi)\}\]
and
\[\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}:=\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau]):\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m_\star,\xi),\ W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}\}.\]

items.label: Definition P-11
items.nl:
Set \(E_P:=\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))\le r_{n,\alpha}\}\) and
\(\rho_{n,\alpha}:=R_{n,\alpha}/m_\star\).  Merge repeated atoms of \(\widehat\lambda_n\), join two distinct support points when their distance is at most \(4\rho_{n,\alpha}\), and let \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) be the resulting connected components.  For \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), define
\[
K_C(P):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\},
\qquad
K_C(\xi):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\xi):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
Rebase the mass interval on the computable outer confidence set:
\[
I_C:=\left[
\inf_{\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi)),
\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi))
\right].
\]
In the ordered-support and transport-plan representation of \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\), both endpoints are values of the same finite union of fixed-dimensional mixed-integer constrained programs: for each \(1\le r\le k\), add variables \(z_a\in\{0,1\}\), impose
\[
z_a=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\min_{c\in C}|x_a-c|\le\rho_{n,\alpha},
\]
and respectively minimize or maximize \(\sum_{a=1}^rw_az_a\) subject to all ordered-support, atom-floor, simplex, and transport constraints in \(\mathrm{def:wasserstein\text{-}confidence\text{-}set}\).  Infimum and supremum are used so that atoms lying exactly on an association boundary are handled by the displayed weak inequality; no claim of an efficient exact solver is made.

The report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) contains, for every component \(C\), the support interval
\([\min C-\rho_{n,\alpha},\max C+\rho_{n,\alpha}]\) and the mass interval \(I_C\).  Finally define
\[
\Delta_C(P):=\inf\{|x-y|:x\in K_C(P),\ y\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\setminus K_C(P)\},
\]
with value \(+\infty\) when the complement is empty.

items.label: Definition P-12
items.nl: Write the positive law estimator uniquely as \(\widehat\nu_n=\sum_{\ell=1}^{\widehat s_n}\widehat w_{\ell,n}\delta_{\widehat\tau_{\ell,n}}\), where \(\widehat\tau_{1,n}<\cdots<\widehat\tau_{\widehat s_n,n}\) and every \(\widehat w_{\ell,n}>0\). If \(\widehat s_n=k\), set \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}:=(\widehat w_{1,n},\ldots,\widehat w_{k,n})\); if \(\widehat s_n<k\), set \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}:=(1/k,\ldots,1/k)\). Ordering the finitely many support points and extracting their jump sizes are Borel operations, so this defines a total Borel map into \(\Delta^{k-1}\) without an undeclared dependence on \(\alpha\).

items.label: Definition P-13
items.nl: For \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), let \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) satisfy \(P(U=1)=0.4\), \(P(U=2)=0.6\), \(P(T=1\mid U=1)=0.4\), \(P(T=1\mid U=2)=0.6\), \(X=(1,X_2)^\top\), \(Z=(1,Z_2)^\top\), \(B=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0.2&0.8\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(A_0=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0.3&0.7\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(A_1=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0.35&0.75\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(E[Y(0)\mid U]=(0.25,0.25)\), and \(E[Y(1)\mid U]=(0.5-\varepsilon,0.5+\varepsilon)\). Conditional on \(U\), draw \(X_2,Y(0),Y(1),T\) mutually independently as Bernoulli variables with the stated conditional means; conditional on \(U,T\), draw \(Z_2\) independently of \((X_2,Y(0),Y(1))\) with mean given by \(A_T\), and set \(Y=Y(T)\).

items.label: Definition P-16
items.nl: For positive-law repair, start from Bauer--Fike localization of the empirical compressed operator, replace individual eigenvectors inside overlapping discs by Kato contour projectors, and transport aggregate projector mass only across each cluster diameter.  At the realized empirical summary only, let \(m=(m_j)_{0\le j<2k}\) be its first \(2k\) spectral moments and choose a valid positive \(k\)-atomic law \(\sum_i w_i\delta_{x_i}\) that globally minimizes the \(L^1\) discrepancy \(\sum_{j=0}^{2k-1}|m_j-\sum_i w_i x_i^j|\) across those first \(2k\) moments over all valid positive \(k\)-atomic laws, before extracting the repaired real probability measure.  This is a projection relation local to that realized summary and does not require a selector or projection map on any other input. For the labeled-weight converse, differentiate the Bernoulli factorization of \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and solve the linear score-cancellation equations for proxy and treatment primitives so that a weight displacement \(h\) preserves the factorization while the observed score has order \(g h\).

items.label: Definition P-17
items.nl:
Let \(D:=4d_zd_x+d_x\), \(b:=4\sqrt{d_zd_x}+\sqrt{d_x}\), and \(\epsilon_n:=n^{-1/2}\).  Partition the coordinate box \([-L,L]^D\) into a deterministic lexicographically ordered grid of half-open cubes of side at most \(\epsilon_n/b\).  If \(\mathscr S\ne\varnothing\), from every cube meeting \(\mathscr S\) fix one representative \(q_{n,\ell}\in\mathscr S\), and let \(\widehat q_n\) be the smallest-index minimizer of \(d_S(q_{n,\ell},\widehat S_n)\).  At \(\widehat q_n\), retain the \(k\) right singular directions of the vertically stacked proxy moment whose singular values exceed \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\), call the resulting basis \(V\), and form the compressed effect operator \(\Delta\), left anchor \(a\), and right anchor \(c\) by the formulas in \(\mathrm{def:compressed\text{-}operator}\).  For each distinct eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(\Delta\), put \(E_\lambda:=\prod_{\gamma\ne\lambda}(\Delta-\gamma I_k)/(\lambda-\gamma)\), with the empty product equal to \(I_k\), and define
\[
\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}:=\sum_{\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\Delta)}a^\top E_\lambda c\,\delta_\lambda.
\]
If \(\mathscr S=\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\) to be the unit point mass at zero.

items.label: Definition P-18
Assumption A-12
items.nl: The positive-mass latent effects \(\tau_u\) take exactly \(k\) distinct values.

items.label: Assumption A-13
items.nl: The Kullback--Leibler divergence from \(P_O\) to the observed margin of the two-class collision witness at perturbation zero is at most \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}/n\).

items.label: Assumption A-14
items.nl: The Kullback--Leibler divergence from \(P_O\) to the observed margin of the two-class witness at perturbation \(g/2\) is at most \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}/n\).

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl:
There is a choice of \(C_0=C_0(k,d_x,d_z,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) such that, for every \(0<\eta<1/2\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))>
 C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\eta)}{n}}\right\}\le \eta.
\]
With \(\eta\) replaced by \(\alpha\), the radius in the display is \(r_{n,\alpha}\).  In addition, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 Q_P^{(n)}\{N_{t,n}=0\}=(1-P(T=t))^n\le(1-k\pi_0)^n.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:arm-mass-lower-bound
items.nl:
Let \(P\) be a full-data law on \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\) with latent cardinality \(k\) satisfying the latent-arm positivity margin \(P(U=u,T=t)\ge\pi_0\) for every \(1\le u\le k\) and every \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  Since the arm \(\{T=t\}\) is the disjoint union of the \(k\) latent-arm cells \(\{U=u,T=t\}\), the observed arm mass obeys
\[
P(T=t)\ge k\pi_0
\]
for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\).

items.label: Lemma lem:observed-proxy-moment-factorization
items.nl:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) with \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), \(L\ge1\) and \(\pi_0>0\).  Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the observable armwise proxy moment factors through the latent-arm weights:
\[
M_t(P)=A_t\Gamma_tB^\top,
\qquad
\Gamma_t:=\operatorname{diag}\left\{\frac{P(U=u,T=t)}{P(T=t)}:1\le u\le k\right\},
\]
where \(A_t\) is the reference-proxy feature matrix and \(B\) is the target-proxy feature matrix.

items.label: Lemma lem:proxy-coordinate-envelopes
items.nl:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) with \(2\le k\) and \(k\le d_x\).  Then, \(P\)-almost surely, all coordinates of the two proxies and of the outcome--reference-proxy product are bounded by the model envelope:
\[
|X_i|\le L\ \ (1\le i\le d_x),
\qquad
|Z_j|\le L\ \ (1\le j\le d_z),
\qquad
|YZ_j|\le L\ \ (1\le j\le d_z).
\]
The first bound is the \(X\)-envelope; the other two follow from the anchor coordinate \(X_{i_0}=1\) together with the operator-norm envelopes on \(ZX^\top\) and \(YZX^\top\).

items.label: Lemma lem:latent-mean-envelope
items.nl:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) with \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), \(k\le d_z\), \(L\ge1\), \(\pi_0>0\) and \(\sigma_0>0\).  Then every latent conditional potential-outcome mean obeys the derived effect-radius bound
\[
|\mu_{tu}|\le \frac{L_\tau}{2},
\qquad 1\le u\le k,\ t\in\{0,1\}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:latent-effect-envelope
items.nl:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) with \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), \(k\le d_z\), \(L\ge1\), \(\pi_0>0\) and \(\sigma_0>0\).  Then every latent-class treatment effect obeys
\[
|\tau_u|=|\mu_{1u}-\mu_{0u}|\le L_\tau,
\qquad 1\le u\le k.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:witness-latent-mass
items.nl:
For every \(\varepsilon\) with \(0\le\varepsilon\le1/8\), the latent-class masses of the two-class Bernoulli witness \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) are
\[
p_1=\frac25,
\qquad
p_2=\frac35 .
\]
In particular they do not depend on \(\varepsilon\) and are unequal.

items.label: Lemma lem:witness-latent-effect
items.nl:
For every \(\varepsilon\) with \(0\le\varepsilon\le1/8\), the latent-class treatment effects of the two-class Bernoulli witness \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) are
\[
\tau_1=\frac14-\varepsilon,
\qquad
\tau_2=\frac14+\varepsilon .
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:witness-observed-arm-mass
items.nl:
For every \(\varepsilon\) with \(0\le\varepsilon\le1/8\), the observed margin of the two-class Bernoulli witness assigns the treatment arms the masses
\[
(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}})_O(T=0)=\frac{12}{25},
\qquad
(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}})_O(T=1)=\frac{13}{25}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:witness-target-feature-determinant
items.nl:
For every \(\varepsilon\) with \(0\le\varepsilon\le1/8\), the target-proxy feature matrix \(B\) of the two-class Bernoulli witness \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) has determinant
\[
\det(B)=\frac35 .
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:witness-reference-feature-determinant
items.nl:
For every \(\varepsilon\) with \(0\le\varepsilon\le1/8\) and each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the reference-proxy feature matrix \(A_t\) of the two-class Bernoulli witness \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) has determinant
\[
\det(A_t)=\frac25 .
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:path-proxy-rank-margin
items.nl: For all \(g\) and \(h\) with \(0\le g\le1/4\) and \(|h|\le1/100\), the path law \(P_{g,h}\) satisfies the proxy-rank margin with \(\sigma_0=1/10\): the reference-proxy feature matrices \(A_0,A_1\) and the target-proxy feature matrix \(B\) formed from \(P_{g,h}\) all have smallest singular value at least \(1/10\).

items.label: Lemma lem:path-model-membership
items.nl: For all \(g\) and \(h\) with \(0\le g\le1/4\) and \(|h|\le1/100\), the path law \(P_{g,h}\) belongs to the uniformly conditioned model class \(\mathcal M\) with constants \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\) and \(\sigma_0=1/10\): it satisfies the core numerical domain for \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), reference-proxy separation, target-proxy separation, consistency, armwise latent ignorability, the anchor condition, the three boundedness envelopes, latent-arm positivity with margin \(1/10\), and the proxy-rank margin with \(\sigma_0=1/10\).

items.label: Lemma lem:path-gap-stratum-membership
items.nl:
For all \(g\) and \(h\) with \(0<g\le1/4\) and \(|h|\le1/100\), the path law \(P_{g,h}\) lies in the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) with constants \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\) and \(\sigma_0=1/10\): it lies in \(\mathcal M\), the gap scale satisfies \(0<g\le1/4\), the smallest positive effect gap obeys the gap window
\[
\frac g2\le\delta(P_{g,h})\le 2g
\]
(indeed \(\delta(P_{g,h})=g\)), and its two latent effects are distinct.

items.label: Lemma lem:path-local-weight-experiment
items.nl:
Fix \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\in(0,1)\), a sample size \(n\), and \(g,h\) with \(0<g\le1/4\), \(|h|\le1/100\) and
\[
16000\,g^2h^2\le\frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) belongs to the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\) with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\) and \(\sigma_0=1/10\): it lies in the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) and its observed margin satisfies the neighborhood bound
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{g,h})_O\,\middle\|\,(P_{g,0})_O\right)\le\frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n},
\qquad
P_{g,0}=P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{g/2}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:ordered-masses-measure-invariance
items.nl: Let \(\xi\) and \(\xi'\) be represented atomic laws with at most \(k\) slots on \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\) that represent the same probability law, that is \(\nu_\xi=\nu_{\xi'}\).  Then their effect-ordered mass vectors coincide.  Consequently the ordered-weight target \(p^{\uparrow}\) depends only on the represented probability law and not on the chosen finite representative.

items.label: Lemma lem:observed-outcome-proxy-moment-factorization
items.nl:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) with \(2\le k\) and \(\pi_0>0\).  Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the observable armwise outcome-weighted proxy moment factors through the latent-arm weights and the latent conditional potential-outcome means:
\[
N_t(P)=A_t\Gamma_t\operatorname{diag}\{\mu_{tu}:1\le u\le k\}B^\top,
\qquad
\Gamma_t:=\operatorname{diag}\left\{\frac{P(U=u,T=t)}{P(T=t)}:1\le u\le k\right\},
\]
where \(A_t\) is the reference-proxy feature matrix and \(B\) is the target-proxy feature matrix.  The identity is obtained from reference-proxy separation, target-proxy separation, causal consistency, latent ignorability, latent-arm positivity, and integrability of each coordinate \(YZ_iX_j\) on every latent-treatment cell.

items.label: Lemma lem:latent-arm-weight-invertibility
items.nl:
Let \(P\) be a full-data probability law satisfying latent-arm positivity with margin \(\pi_0>0\).  Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the diagonal matrix of normalized latent-arm weights
\[
\Gamma_t=\operatorname{diag}\left\{\frac{P(U=u,T=t)}{P(T=t)}:1\le u\le k\right\}
\]
is injective as a linear map on \(\mathbb R^k\), hence invertible.

items.label: Lemma lem:moore-penrose-product-cancellation
items.nl:
Let \(C\) and \(B\) be real matrices with \(k\) columns, each of full column rank \(k\), and let \(\mu\in\mathbb R^k\).  Then
\[
(CB^\top)^\dagger\bigl(C\operatorname{diag}(\mu)B^\top\bigr)
=
(B^\dagger)^\top\operatorname{diag}(\mu)B^\top .
\]
In particular, taking \(C=A_t\Gamma_t\), \(B\) the target-proxy feature matrix, and \(\mu=(\mu_{t1},\ldots,\mu_{tk})\), the two arm factorizations \(M_t(P)=A_t\Gamma_tB^\top\) and \(N_t(P)=A_t\Gamma_t\operatorname{diag}\{\mu_{tu}\}_{u=1}^kB^\top\) yield the Moore--Penrose cancellation
\[
M_t(P)^\dagger N_t(P)=(B^\dagger)^\top\operatorname{diag}\{\mu_{tu}\}_{u=1}^kB^\top .
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:summary-metric-coordinate-comparison
items.nl:
Equip the ambient five-block summary space with its coordinate Euclidean distance \(\rho_{\mathrm{sum}}\).  Then, for all observable moment summaries \(s\) and \(s'\),
\[
d_S(s,s')\le\Lambda_{\mathrm{sum}}\,\rho_{\mathrm{sum}}(s,s'),
\qquad
\Lambda_{\mathrm{sum}}:=4\operatorname{Ent}_{d_z,d_x}+d_x,
\]
where \(\operatorname{Ent}_{r,c}\) denotes the entrywise-to-operator norm constant for \(r\times c\) matrices.

items.label: Lemma lem:summary-metric-continuity
items.nl: The summary metric is jointly continuous for the ambient coordinate topology on the five-block summary space: the map \((s,s')\mapsto d_S(s,s')\) is continuous.  In particular, if \(q_m\to q\) and \(q'_m\to q'\) in the coordinate topology, then \(d_S(q_m,q'_m)\to d_S(q,q')\), so a \(d_S\)-control valid on the admissible summary image \(\mathscr S\) passes to every point of its coordinate closure \(\mathcal K\).

items.label: Lemma lem:stacked-proxy-moment-signal-margin
items.nl:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) with \(2\le k\le d_x\), \(L\ge1\), \(\pi_0>0\), and \(\sigma_0>0\).  Then the vertically stacked observable proxy moment retains the quantitative signal margin
\[
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2
\le
\sigma_{k-1}\{\operatorname{stack}(M_0(P),M_1(P))\},
\]
with zero-based singular-value indexing.

items.label: Lemma lem:model-compressed-spectral-certificate
Lemma lem:diagonalization-condition-number-bound
items.nl:
Let \(d_x\ge1\) and \(k\ge1\), let \(B\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\) be a target-proxy feature matrix admitting a thin signal factorization \(B=V\Upsilon\) with \(V^\top V=I_k\) and \(\Upsilon\) invertible, and let \(\tau\in\mathbb R^k\).  Assume the entry bounds \(|B_{iu}|\le L\) with \(L\ge0\) and \(|(\Upsilon^{-1})_{ru}|\le\sigma_0^{-1}\) with \(\sigma_0>0\).  Put
\[
K_{\mathrm{forw}}:=\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\sigma_0^{-1}+\bigl(\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}+\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\bigr),
\qquad
K_{\mathrm{back}}:=\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}(d_xL)+\bigl(\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}+\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\bigr),
\qquad
\kappa_\star:=\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}^{\,2}K_{\mathrm{forw}}K_{\mathrm{back}},
\]
where \(\operatorname{Ent}_{r,c}\) is the entrywise-to-operator norm constant of \cref{obj:lem:summary-metric-coordinate-comparison}.  Then the ambient basis change \(\mathcal A:=V(\Upsilon^{-1})^\top V^\top+(I_{d_x}-VV^\top)\) and its inverse \(\mathcal A^{-1}=V\Upsilon^\top V^\top+(I_{d_x}-VV^\top)\) satisfy \(\|\mathcal A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le K_{\mathrm{forw}}\) and \(\|\mathcal A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le K_{\mathrm{back}}\), and the real diagonalization of \((B^\dagger)^\top\operatorname{diag}(\tau)B^\top\) whose eigenbasis matrix \(R\) has columns \(\mathcal Au_j\) for an orthonormal extension \((u_j)_{j=1}^{d_x}\) of the columns of \(V\) has condition number at most \(\kappa_\star\):
\[
\|R\|_{\mathrm{op}}\,\|R^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\kappa_\star .
\]

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl:
Every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfies, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(T=t)&\ge k\pi_0,\\
M_t(P)&=A_t\operatorname{diag}\{P(U=u\mid T=t):1\le u\le k\}B^\top,\\
\sigma_k\{M_t(P)V(P)\}&=\sigma_k\{M_t(P)\}\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\\
\sigma_k\!\left(\begin{bmatrix}M_0(P)\\M_1(P)\end{bmatrix}\right)&\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2,
\end{aligned}
\qquad
\lVert M_t(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},\ \lVert N_t(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},\ \lVert m_X(P)\rVert_2\le L.
\]
Define \(L_{\tau}:=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\).  The retained assumptions further imply, for every \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
|Y(t)|\le L_{\tau}/2\quad P\text{-almost surely conditional on }U=u,
\qquad |\mu_{tu}|\le L_{\tau}/2,
\qquad |\tau_u|\le L_{\tau}.
\]
With the fixed dimensions and anchor normalization, \(\mathcal M\) is a quantitatively uniform conditional-moment subclass of the published VMW parameter class.  It retains VMW Assumption 1 in its exact armwise form, including \(Y(t)\perp T\mid U\) separately for each \(t\), and strengthens the published qualitative latent positivity and full-rank requirements to the fixed margins \(\pi_0\) and \(\sigma_0\).  It imposes no additional latent conditional-moment or potential-outcome support assumption: the displayed potential-outcome envelope is derived from proxy rank, the observable envelopes, reference-proxy separation, consistency, armwise ignorability, and latent--arm positivity.  The converse inclusion and all upper, confidence, cluster, and full-class matching conclusions on the full published VMW class are not asserted; only lower bounds carried by explicit witness paths transfer upward to containing classes.

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl: The admissible summary image \(\mathscr S=S(\mathcal M)\) is uniformly bounded under \(d_S\). Hence its closure \(\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S}\) is a compact subset of the finite-dimensional summary space. Moreover, \(\mathcal K\) is nonempty if and only if \(\mathcal M\) is nonempty.

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl: There is a finite \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) such that, for every \(P,P'\in\mathcal M\), \[W_1(\nu_P,\nu_{P'})\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}d_S(S(P),S(P')).\] Equivalently, \(F\) is \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}\)-Lipschitz on \(\mathscr S\) and has a unique extension \(\overline F:\mathcal K\to\mathcal P_k([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}])\) satisfying \[W_1(\overline F(q),\overline F(q'))\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}d_S(q,q'),\qquad q,q'\in\mathcal K.\] The bound is uniform over every multiplicity pattern and simultaneous support merge or split, contains no inverse power of \(\delta(P)\) or \(\delta(P')\), and the extension always returns a positive real probability measure, including after projection of an empirical summary whose raw compressed operator has nonreal eigenvalues.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
If \(\mathcal K
e\varnothing\), a Borel nearest-point selector \(\Pi(s)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in\mathcal K}d_S(q,s)\) exists by Brown and Purves (1973), and \(\widehat
u_n=\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n))\). If \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), the corrected fallback definitions set \(\Pi(s)=0\), \(\widehat
u_n=\delta_0\), and \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}=\{\delta_0\}\). Consequently, in either case \(\widehat
u_n\) is a total Borel positive real law-valued estimator and \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) is nonempty on every sample.

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl:
The explicit sample-evaluable lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) and the theoretical nearest-summary estimator \(\widehat\nu_n=\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n))\) both estimate the quotient law at a collision-uniform root-\(n\) rate.  Specifically, there is a finite \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) such that, for every \(0<\eta<1/2\),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{
\max\{W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P),W_1(\widehat\nu_n,\nu_P)\}
>C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}\right\}\le\eta.
\]
Both estimators are total, Borel, positive, and real-law-valued on every sample.  The first is computable by the explicit no-advice finite lattice in \(\mathrm{prop:polynomial\text{-}net\text{-}law\text{-}estimator}\); the second remains the closure-based theoretical construction used for statements requiring membership in \(\overline F(\mathcal K)\).  The simultaneous bound includes \(\{N_{t,n}=0\}\), whose probability is at most \((1-k\pi_0)^n\) for each arm, and is uniform over every effect multiplicity pattern.

items.label: Theorem T-6
items.nl:
For a suitable choice of the simultaneous-concentration constant in \(r_{n,\alpha}\), both the original summary-inversion set and the computable outer set are honest:
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}\{
\nu_P\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\}
\ge1-\alpha.
\]
Both sets are nonempty on every sample, and
\[
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
\le4C_{\mathrm{mod}}r_{n,\alpha},
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha})
\le2R_{n,\alpha}.
\]
The second set has the explicit fixed-dimensional constrained-program representation in \(\mathrm{def:wasserstein\text{-}confidence\text{-}set}\).  Coverage and root-\(n\) \(W_1\)-diameter are uniform over every collision, merge, and split stratum; neither equality nor inclusion between the two confidence sets is claimed.

items.label: Theorem T-7
items.nl:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), on \(E_P\), the sets \(K_C(P)\), indexed by \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) constructed from \(\widehat\lambda_n\), form a partition of \(\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\).  Every \(K_C(P)\) lies in the reported support interval for \(C\), and \(I_C\), computed over \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\), contains \(\nu_P(K_C(P))\).  More explicitly, a singleton associated cluster has support-interval length at most
\[
4\rho_{n,\alpha}=4R_{n,\alpha}/m_\star,
\]
its mass interval has length at most
\[
\frac{8}{m_\star}\min\!\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\delta(P)}\right\},
\]
and every associated cluster satisfies
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_C)
\le\frac{8}{m_\star}\min\!\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\Delta_C(P)}\right\},
\]
where the right side is interpreted as zero when \(\Delta_C(P)=+\infty\).  Finally,
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}(E_P)\ge1-\alpha.
\]
Thus the entire report has a fixed-dimensional constrained-program representation, while effects unresolved at the \(\rho_{n,\alpha}\) scale are pooled without hiding the true-cluster association or its external gap.

items.label: Theorem T-8
items.nl: As a labeled-coordinate consequence of the root-law estimator and the additional gap-local regime, there is a finite \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) such that, uniformly over \(g\in(0,1/4]\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(g)}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\lVert\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}-p^{\uparrow}(P)\rVert_1\right]\le C\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.\] The inverse-gap behavior concerns ordered labels and does not enter the \(W_1\) risk of \(\nu_P\).

items.label: Theorem T-9
items.nl: For every \(0\le\varepsilon\le1/8\), with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\), the law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\). It satisfies \(P(T=0)=0.48\), \(P(T=1)=0.52\), \(\det(B)=0.6\), \(\det(A_0)=\det(A_1)=0.4\), \(\det(M_0(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=0.06\), \(\det(M_1(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=0.4\cdot0.6\cdot36/169\), and \(\nu_{P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}}=0.4\delta_{0.25-\varepsilon}+0.6\delta_{0.25+\varepsilon}\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), all proxy matrices remain nonsingular, the quotient law is \(\delta_{0.25}\), and the latent weights remain unequal.

For the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\), there are a sufficiently small universal amplitude \(a>0\) and constants \(c,C>0\) such that \[\inf_{\widetilde
u_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_n^{

The quotient-law path has one-observation Kullback--Leibler divergence at most \(C/n\) and \(W_1\)-separation at least \(c/\sqrt n\). For the labeled path, a weight displacement \(h\) preserves both proxy conditional-independence factorizations, positivity, and rank, has one-observation observed-data Kullback--Leibler divergence at most \(C g^2h^2\), and has ordered-weight separation at least \(c|h|\); taking \(|h|=a\min\{1,(\sqrt n g)^{-1}\}\) gives the second bound.

items.label: Theorem T-11
items.nl:
For the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\), the upper and lower bounds on the same uniformly conditioned causal VMW class imply that, for finite \(0<c<C<\infty\),
\[
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}\le\inf_{\widetilde\nu_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[W_1(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P)]\le\frac{C}{\sqrt n}.
\]

items.label: Theorem T-12
items.nl:
For the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\), uniformly for \(g\in(0,1/4]\), the labeled upper and lower bounds on the same gap stratum imply that, for finite \(0<c<C<\infty\),
\[
c\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}\le\inf_{\widetilde p_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(g)}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\lVert\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\rVert_1]\le C\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]

items.label: Theorem T-13
items.nl:
In the fixed-dimensional exact-real computational model in which the class-dependent finite library of representative summaries is precomputed, \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\) is a total Borel map with values in the positive real probability laws having at most \(k\) atoms.  The library has cardinality at most
\[
C\,n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2},
\]
and exhaustive nearest-library search, including formation of \(\widehat S_n\), uses at most \(C\{n+n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2}\}\) fixed-dimensional arithmetic, comparison, singular-value, and fixed-degree root-isolation operations.  Singular-value thresholding at \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) retains exactly the \(k\)-dimensional signal space for every stored representative and remains correct under operator perturbations smaller than \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\).  For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), the deterministic inequality
\[
W_1(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}},\nu_P)
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\left\{2d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}\right\}
\]
holds.  Consequently this explicit finite-library estimator has a collision-uniform root-\(n\) high-probability guarantee, without diagonalizing a possibly nonreal empirical compressed spectrum.

items.label: Theorem T-14
items.nl:
Fix \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\).  There exist a sufficiently small universal \(a>0\) and a universal \(c>0\) such that the following holds for every \(n\ge1\).  Let \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) be any parameter class in the published structural/finite-regularity VMW model satisfying \(\{P_0^{\mathrm{wit}},P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\}\subseteq\mathcal V_n^\nu\).  For \(g\in(0,1/4]\), set \(h(n,g):=a\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\}\), using the admissible positive orientation of the factorization-preserving path \(P_{g,h}\), and let \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}\) be any published-VMW parameter class satisfying \(\{P_{g,0},P_{g,h(n,g)}\}\subseteq\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}\).  Then
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\nu_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[W_1(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P)]\ge\frac c{\sqrt n}
\]
and, uniformly in \(g\in(0,1/4]\),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde p_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\lVert\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\rVert_1]
\ge c\min\left\{1,\frac1{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]
Only witness-pair containment is required; neither comparator class need contain the corresponding entire local neighborhood.  The quotient pair lies in the published structural/finite-regularity VMW model, while its collision point \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) is outside the separated simple-effect recovery class of VMW Theorem 7.2; the labeled pair is separated.  This two-point transfer does not extend the gap-free modulus, either estimator upper bound, either confidence guarantee, either cluster guarantee, or either matching minimax conclusion beyond \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal M(g)\).

items.label: Theorem T-15
items.nl:
Put \(m_\star:=\pi_0\), \(s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2\),
\[
H_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil+\lceil\pi_0^{-1}\rceil+2k
+\lceil4\sqrt{d_xk}\rceil+\lceil2k/\sigma_0\rceil,
\qquad q_n:=H_n^{-1},
\]
and \(\ell_n:=\lceil m_\star H_n\rceil\).  For a rectangular matrix \(G=\sum_j\sigma_j u_jv_j^\top\), define
\[
G^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top,
\qquad
\widehat D_n:=(\widehat M_{1,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{1,n}
-(\widehat M_{0,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{0,n}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal V_n\) consist of the polar factors \(G(G^\top G)^{-1/2}\) of all \(G\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{d_x\times k}\) with \(|G_{ij}|\le1\) and \(\sigma_k(G)\ge1/2\).  Let \(\mathcal R_n\) consist of all \(R\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{k\times k}\) with \(\sigma_k(R)\ge\sigma_0/2\) and \(\lVert R\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\sqrt{k}L\), and set
\[
\mathcal P_n:=\left\{H_n^{-1}(a_1,\ldots,a_k)^\top:
a_u\in\{\ell_n,\ldots,H_n\},\ \sum_{u=1}^ka_u=H_n\right\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal T_n\) be the \(k\)-fold product of the clipped \(q_n\)-lattice in \([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]\).  For \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n\), define
\[
D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,
\quad m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p,
\quad b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1,
\quad \lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^kp_u\delta_{\tau_u},
\]
and
\[
J_n(\vartheta):=\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert m_\vartheta-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2
+\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf1_k\rVert_2.
\]
Order the finite product lattice lexicographically, let \(\widehat\vartheta_n\) be its first minimizer of \(J_n\), and define the explicit estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n:=\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n}\).  Every distinct atom of \(\widehat\lambda_n\) has mass at least \(m_\star\).

The following displayed constants are valid and depend only on the fixed class parameters.  With
\[
\begin{aligned}
c_V&:=4\sqrt{d_xk},
&K_D&:=\frac{4\sqrt{k}LL_{\tau}}{\sigma_0},
&A_D&:=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\\
K_f&:=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},
&c_D&:=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}LL_{\tau}}{\sigma_0^2}
+\frac{2\sqrt{k}L}{\sigma_0}+\frac{kL_{\tau}}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m&:=2\sqrt{k}Lc_V+k+kL,
&c_b&:=k+2\sqrt{k}Lc_V,
&c_{\mathrm{grid}}&:=c_D+c_m+c_b,\\
B_{\mathrm{lat}}&:=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}},
&&
C_{\mathrm{lat}}&:=\max\!\left\{\frac{8L_{\tau}}{s_0},
(L_{\tau}+K_D+LK_f)B_{\mathrm{lat}}\right\},
\end{aligned}
\]
one has, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every \(n\ge1\), and every sample,
\[
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P)
\le C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]
The rule is a total Borel map on every empirical summary, including empty-arm summaries and summaries whose raw compressed operator has nonreal eigenvalues, to a positive real law with at most \(k\) atoms in \([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]\).  It uses no precomputed admissible-summary representative.  In the fixed-dimensional unit-cost exact-real model its candidate list has cardinality at most \(C n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2}\), and exhaustive minimization has polynomial runtime in \(n\).  Consequently, for a finite \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) and every \(0<\eta<1/2\),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P)>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}\right\}\le\eta.
\tag{12}
\]

items.label: Cited result lem:vmw-model-scope
items.nl: In the published VMW model, Assumption 1 includes \(Z\perp(X,Y)\mid(T,U)\), \(X\perp(Y,T)\mid U\), causal consistency \(Y=Y(T)\), and latent ignorability \(Y(t)\perp T\mid U\).  Assumption 2 requires \(A_0,A_1,B\) to have full column rank \(k\), and Section 4.2 uses strict latent positivity \(P(T=t\mid U=u)>0\).  These are qualitative conditions: the source does not impose the fixed margins \(\pi_0\) and \(\sigma_0\) used to define \(\mathcal M\).

items.label: Cited result lem:vmw-separated-recovery-scope
items.nl: For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z\) and a population law \(P\), write \(M_{ZX\mid t}(P):=E_P[ZX^\top\mid T=t]\), \(M_{\mathrm{stack}}(P):=[M_{ZX\mid 0}(P)^\top,M_{ZX\mid 1}(P)^\top]^\top\), and let \(V_k(P)\) be an orthonormal basis for the population \(k\)-dimensional right singular subspace of \(M_{\mathrm{stack}}(P)\).  VMW Assumption 4 is the law-level requirement that there exist finite positive constants \(L_X,L_{ZX},L_{ZXY}\) for which \(\lVert X\rVert_2\le L_X\), \(\lVert ZX^\top\rVert_2\le L_{ZX}\), and \(\lVert YZX^\top\rVert_2\le L_{ZXY}\) almost surely under \(P\), while \(\pi(P):=\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}P(T=t)>0\) and \(\sigma(P):=\min\{\sigma_k(M_{\mathrm{stack}}(P)),\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}\sigma_k(M_{ZX\mid t}(P)V_k(P))\}>0\).  It subsequently defines \(M_X,M_Y,\kappa_B,\Gamma_X,\Gamma_Y\), and \(\kappa_{ZX}^{\star}\) as fixed derived conditioning quantities, not as additional conjunctive assumptions.  VMW Theorem 7.2 operates under the standing Assumption 1 conditions \(Z\perp(X,Y)\mid(T,U)\), \(X\perp(Y,T)\mid U\), causal consistency \(Y=Y(T)\), and latent ignorability \(Y(t)\perp T\mid U\), together with the anchor normalization \(X_1=1\) almost surely.  It additionally assumes Assumption 2, strict latent positivity, Assumption 4, and spectral separation, where spectral separation means \(\tau(u)\ne\tau(v)\) for distinct \(u,v\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and is vacuous for \(k=1\).  Together with its stated \(n,\eta\)-dependent sample-size and radius conditions, the theorem gives simultaneous high-probability finite-sample recovery of the treatment effects, the anchor-normalized feature matrix, and the simplex-projected mixture weights.  Consequently, when \(k\ge2\), a treatment-effect collision lies outside the separated recovery regime of VMW Theorem 7.2.
